page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that this instance delivers modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 20.19 GB/sec (bottom 10%) and write large block bandwidth at 18.14 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Geekbench scores align with this trend, placing both single-core (918.0) and multi-core (1990.0) performance in the bottom 10% of tested instances.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.xlarge is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio relative to its processing throughput. While it offers a generous 32.0 GB of RAM, the underlying Intel Xeon processor and memory subsystem exhibit lower transfer rates and processing speeds. This makes the instance a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without demanding high-throughput computational power or rapid memory access speeds.

Given these characteristics, the ecs.se1.xlarge is suited for memory-intensive but computationally light workloads. Appropriate use cases include caching layers, small-scale database operations, basic web serving, and lightweight text or image processing tasks that fit entirely within the 32.0 GB memory space but do not require high CPU performance.
